data.gender_notes: Valera is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Valera is derived from the Greek name Valerius, meaning 'healthy, strong, or powerful'. In ancient Rome, Valerius was a common surname for soldiers and military leaders, suggesting a connection to bravery and strength. The name Valera carries the meaning “Powerful, valiant” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Valera usually hope their child will grow to embody powerful, valiant and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes strength and courage in the face of adversity.
